chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from al-Yasa' who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: There is no divorce except upon the Sunnah, and there is no divorce upon the Sunnah except during a period of purity (tuhr) without copulation, and there is no divorce upon the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation except with witnesses; and if a man divorced according to the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation, but did not have it witnessed, his divorce would not be a (valid) divorce; and if a man divorced according to the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation, and had it witnessed, but did not intend the divorce, his divorce would not be a (valid) divorce.

key_terms.السنة: al-Sunnah — here meaning the proper prophetic method for performing divorce, as opposed to bid'i (innovated) divorce
key_terms.بينة: Bayyina — clear proof; here specifically two just witnesses who must be present at the pronouncement of talaq
key_terms.جماع: Jima' — sexual intercourse; if it occurred during the current tuhr period, divorce is invalid until after the next menses
key_terms.طلاق: Talaq — the Islamic legal act of divorce/repudiation, initiated by the husband
key_terms.طهر: Tuhr — the period between two menstrual cycles during which a woman is in a state of ritual purity; a required condition for talaq
key_terms.نية: Niyyah — intention; an internal mental act required for the validity of any legal act in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce (talaq) in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) enumerates three essential conditions for a valid Shia divorce (talaq): it must conform to the Sunnah, it must be pronounced during the wife's period of ritual purity (tuhr) free from any sexual intercourse since the last menses, and it must be witnessed by two just witnesses. The addition of the third case — where all external conditions are met but the husband lacks genuine intention (niyyah) — reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal acts require sincere intent to be valid. This hadith served early jurists as a foundational source for the law of divorce in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Zurara, from Al Yas’a who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no divorce except upon the Sunnah, and there is no divorce upon the Sunnah except upon purity from without copulation, and there is no divorce upon Sunnah, and upon purity without copulation except with proof (two witnesses); and if a man were to divorce upon Sunnah, and upon purity from without copulation, and does not have it witnessed, his divorce would not happen to be a divorce; and if a man were to divorce upon Sunnah, and upon purity from without copulation, and have it witnessed, and did not intend the divorce, his divorce would not happen to be a divorce’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu Najran from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from al-Yasa’ who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘Divorce, which is not according to Sunnah, is not a divorce. A divorce is not according to Sunnah if it is not pronounced in the presence of two just witnesses, in a menses-free period in which the husband has not gone to bed with her. If a man divorces his wife in a menses-free period during which he has not gone to bed with her but it is not in presence (of two just) witnesses, such divorce is not a valid divorce. If a man divorces his wife according to Sunnah, in a menses-free period in which he has not gone to bed with her and pronounces it in the presence of witnesses but has not intended it to be a divorce it also is not a valid divorce.’”
